notes:
I found no real disagreement between Protestant traditions on Joshua 16. Almost every source reads it as a list of borders that ends with Ephraim's failure at Gezer (v. 10). The disagreements are between individual commentators, mainly on v. 10. I ran out of searches before finding anything from Catholic or Orthodox sites, the NET Bible notes, or prosperity and word-of-faith teachers, so those parts are mostly missing.

---

**v. 1**
- **"Lot":** The Hebrew means the lot "came forth," that is, out of the urn (Pulpit). Gill says this was the next lot drawn after Judah's, because the government being Judah's, and the birthright Joseph's, 1 Chronicles 5:2. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/16-1.htm
- **Why Joseph comes second:** Ellicott says the tribes were always ranked Judah first and Joseph second. Benson sees God's providence in Joseph's lot coming next to Judah's, because Joseph inherited the firstborn's double portion. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/16-1.htm
- **"Waters of Jericho":** Cambridge places this at the spring Ain es-Sultan, the water Elisha healed (2 Kgs 2:19). https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/16-1.htm
- **"The wilderness":** Pulpit identifies it with the wilderness of Beth-aven in Josh 18:12. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/16-1.htm
- **One lot, later divided:** JFB says Joseph's land was drawn as one lot so the two brother tribes would be next to each other, and only the southern border is given here. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/16-1.htm Wesley (Methodist) says the same. https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-book-of-joshua/
- **Bethel:** Bethel means "house of God," where Jacob saw the ladder, so Joseph's sons now inherit the ground of the patriarchs' story. https://biblehub.com/joshua/16-1.htm Gaebelein reads it as a picture: Joseph's lot runs from the Jordan, "the river of death, up to Bethel, which means 'the house of God.'" https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/gab/joshua-16.html

**v. 2**
- **"Bethel (that is, Luz)":** Utley says the Hebrew seems to treat Bethel and Luz as two towns, though other passages say they are two names for one city (Josh 18:13; Gen 28:19). https://bible.org/seriespage/joshua-16 The NKJV footnote says the Septuagint reads "Bethel (that is, Luz)." https://www.blueletterbible.org/nkjv/jos/16/1/
- **Archites:** Utley notes that one of David's counsellors came from this clan (2 Sam 15:32), but apart from that the clan, which was not Israelite, is unknown. https://bible.org/seriespage/joshua-16
- **Places:** Ellicott identifies Archi as 'Ain 'Arik and Ataroth as Ed-Darieh. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/16-1.htm

**v. 3**
- **Places:** In Ellicott, the Japhletites are unidentified, Beth-horon is Beit 'Ur, and Gezer is Tell Jezer. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/16-1.htm The Japhletites are as unknown as the Archites (Utley). https://bible.org/seriespage/joshua-16
- **The coast:** Coffman notes that Dan also seems to have had towns near Joppa, so it shared this stretch of coast with Ephraim. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bcc/joshua-16.html
- **Gezer:** The city was later given with its pasture lands to the Kohathite Levites (Josh 21:21). https://classic.net.bible.org/dictionary.php/dictionary.php?word=GEZER

**v. 4**
- **Order of names:** Manasseh, the firstborn, is named first here, although Jacob put Ephraim first when he blessed them (Gen 48:5). https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-16-commentary Coffman says Ephraim's border is still described first because the birthright passed to him. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bcc/joshua-16.html
- **"Took their inheritance":** Wesley says Judah and Joseph settled before the other tribes to protect the main camp at Gilgal. https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-book-of-joshua/ Poole suggests the phrase means the two tribes split one shared lot between themselves. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/16-4.htm
- **Application:** BibleHub's study notes read the land as a picture of the believer's lasting inheritance (1 Pet 1:4). Receiving it had to be matched by actually occupying it (Judg 1:27-29). https://biblehub.com/joshua/16-4.htm

**v. 5**
- **"On the east":** Ellicott admits these words are hard to explain. If his identifications are right, the line actually runs north and separates Ephraim from Dan. https://biblehub.com/joshua/16-5.htm Wesley takes it as the north-east side. https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-book-of-joshua/
- **"Inheritance":** Precept Austin says the switch from "allotment" to "inheritance" stresses that God himself arranged the gift. It adds that this was Joshua's own tribe. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-16-commentary
- **Beth-horon:** BibleHub links the Beth-horon pass to Joshua's hailstone victory in Josh 10, so the border recalls a past rescue by God. https://biblehub.com/joshua/16-5.htm

**v. 6**
- **Taanath-shiloh:** Utley says this is a different town from Shiloh, where the tabernacle stood, and cites Eusebius and Jerome. https://bible.org/seriespage/joshua-16
- **Unclear places:** Wesley says it is no surprise these borders are obscure now, since they were plain to Israel at the time. https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-book-of-joshua/

**v. 7**
- **"Reached Jericho":** Wesley says this means Jericho's surrounding land, not the city, which belonged to Benjamin (18:21). https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-book-of-joshua/

**v. 8**
- **Tappuah and Kanah:** Tappuah marks the western edge and Kanah is a ravine. Precept Austin puts Ephraim's land at about 38 miles east to west and 20 miles north to south. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-16-commentary

**v. 9**
- **Grammar:** Barnes, Cambridge and Pulpit say the KJV's "were" should be dropped. Verse 9 simply adds the separate towns to Ephraim's inheritance. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/16-9.htm
- **Why Ephraim got towns inside Manasseh:** This is one of the main places commentators disagree.
  - **Ephraim was too big for its land:** Barnes thinks Ephraim's land proved too small, and Manasseh was made up for it from Issachar's and Asher's land. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/16-10.htm Calvin says the towns were deducted to give Ephraim its fair share, and Ephraim did not hold them on an insecure footing among Manasseh's people. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/joshua-16.html Poole, the Geneva Bible and Wesley all say Ephraim was much larger than half of Manasseh. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/16-9.htm https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-book-of-joshua/
  - **Ephraim's ambition:** Coffman, drawing on Hosea, blames the arrogance and ambition of Ephraim. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bcc/joshua-16.html
  - **Unity of the two tribes:** Precept Austin suggests it may have been meant to keep the two tribes united but admits this is a guess. Grant notes that Manasseh also had towns outside its borders (17:11). https://www.preceptaustin.org/pdf/62608/
  - **Later history:** Pulpit thinks it helps explain why the ten northern tribes held together against Judah. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/16-9.htm

**v. 10**
- **Could not, or would not?** This is the biggest disagreement.
  - **Could not:** Keil & Delitzsch say Ephraim could not drive them out and read this the same way as Judah's failure at Jerusalem (15:63). https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/16-10.htm
  - **Would not:** Pulpit contrasts the two. Judah was unable at Jerusalem, but Ephraim apparently chose the easier course of taxing the Canaanites over destroying them. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/16-10.htm Enduring Word argues that if they could make Gezer's people forced labourers, they could have defeated them, especially as Joshua had already conquered Gezer. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/joshua-15-16-17/
  - **Several possibilities:** Gill says either God withheld victory because of their sins, or they were lazy, or they were greedy for tribute, which fits Ephraim's character in Hosea 12:8. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/16-10.htm Matthew Henry suggests carelessness, cowardice, or a lack of faith and zeal. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/16-10.html
- **Was Gezer conquered?** Ligonier says Joshua defeated Gezer's king and army (10:33) but never took the city itself. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/israels-southern-campaign Enduring Word, as above, treats Gezer as already conquered. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/joshua-15-16-17/
- **Why it matters:** JFB calls this the first mention of Israel's "fatal policy" of ignoring the command in Deut 20:16. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/16-10.htm Enduring Word quotes G. Campbell Morgan: Ephraim's sad history began here. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/joshua-15-16-17/
- **What happened later:** Poole and Gill say the Canaanites stayed in Gezer until Solomon's time, when Pharaoh took the city and gave it to his daughter (1 Kgs 9:16). https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/16-10.htm The Septuagint adds a long clause saying exactly this (Calvin's note). https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/joshua-16.html
- **"To this day" and when Joshua was written:**
  - Gill argues the phrase shows the book was written before Solomon. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/16-10.htm
  - Utley says it shows a later editor. He also cites R. K. Harrison's point that scholars should tell occupying a land apart from subduing it, which removes the supposed conflict between Joshua and Judges. https://bible.org/seriespage/joshua-16
  - Coffman rejects critics such as Woudstra who use the verse to argue for a late date. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/16-10.html
- **Application:** BibleHub compares the Canaanites left in Gezer to sins we tolerate and think we control (Eph 4:27). https://biblehub.com/q/Lessons_from_Joshua_16_10_on_resisting_sin.htm The Biblical Illustrator says they may have failed from weakness or greed, and that neglecting God's will for convenience always brings suffering. https://biblehub.com/sermons/joshua/16-10.htm

---

**Gaps**
- **Other views:**
  - **Modern scholarship:** All I found is Utley's "later editor" remark and the dating debate under v. 10.
  - **Catholic:** I only saw the Douay-Rheims wording, "slew not... paying tribute," at https://biblehub.com/joshua/16-10.htm. BibleHub links a Haydock Catholic commentary that I didn't get to read.
  - **Orthodox, NET Bible notes, popular modern teaching:** Nothing found.
- **Traditions:** The pages I read only identify Wesley's tradition (Methodist). I haven't labelled the others with a tradition, because the pages don't state it.
